The Convistelle manifesto

A point of view. A proof of thought.

Convistelle manifesto and pilot guide · Version 0.1 · 17 September 2026

The future is uncertain. Your original view should be clear. What did you expect? How confident were you? What would settle the question? And what happened next?

Convistelle is a forecast observatory for those questions. Inspect a question on Robinhood Chain testnet, choose YES or NO, record your confidence with your own wallet, and return to the outcome. No deposits. No wagering. No payouts. A public record preserves what you submitted; it does not prove that the view is true.

1. The conversation deserves a memory

Market conversation moves quickly. A thoughtful call can disappear between memes and the next headline. A confident claim can be remembered more clearly than the uncertainty that came with it. Screenshots capture moments, but rarely the full story.

We want a better habit: make the question precise, put a view on record before the deadline, and revisit it when the answer becomes knowable. A useful record includes wrong calls, unresolved questions, and cancellations. Its purpose is to improve judgment—not to make every forecast look good.

The idea starts with communities. Independent minds should be able to disagree without losing the context of the discussion. A shared question becomes a meeting point. Everyone chooses their own answer. The record stays available for reflection.

2. Three actions, one complete loop

Discover

Browse the forecast board without connecting a wallet. Read the question, closing time, source and resolution rules. Understand exactly which instrument or event is being observed and what counts as YES. If the rules are unclear, do not submit a call.

Commit

Connect an Ethereum-compatible browser wallet, switch to Robinhood Chain testnet and sign a free message to demonstrate wallet control in this browser session. Choose YES or NO and confidence from 50% to 100% in that side. Then approve a separate onchain transaction. A confirmed transaction creates the record; a connection or message signature alone does not.

Your wallet needs testnet ETH for gas. Convistelle does not ask for a seed phrase, private key, asset deposit or token approval. A rejected wallet request does not create a forecast. The transaction link is the receipt to check.

Reflect

After the question closes, the pilot operator publishes YES, NO or CANCELLED. Your wallet's record shows total calls, resolved calls, correct calls and cancellations. Cancelled calls are excluded from resolved/correct counts. A new question starts the next cycle.

In the pilot, a wallet can submit one immutable call per question and at most 256 calls to this contract. A new wallet is not proof of a new person, so wallet counts must not be described as verified human users.

3. What the pilot actually supports

Available in this release What that means
Public forecast board Questions and state are read from the deployed testnet registry. If RPC reads fail, clearly marked examples replace live interaction.
Wallet verification A signed message is checked in your current browser session. There is no hosted account database or persistent login account.
Onchain forecasts A successful transaction records wallet, question ID, side, confidence and timestamp.
Immutable questions and calls Question text, source and deadline cannot be edited after creation; a confirmed call cannot be changed or deleted through this contract.
Owner resolution The contract owner can create questions and, after their deadline, resolve each once as YES, NO or CANCELLED.
Wallet record Contract reads return the full bounded record, including wrong outcomes and cancelled questions.
Shareable question links Copy a link so someone else can inspect the same question and make an independent call.

The initial questions concern Bitcoin, Ethereum and Robinhood Chain testnet activity. An explicitly named operational test demonstrates the transaction-to-resolution path; it is an engineering check, not customer adoption or forecasting performance.

The pilot does not include monetary stakes, a trading engine, automated copy trading, private community workspaces, Telegram/Discord bots, paid subscriptions, an API service, or automated oracle resolution. There is no announced token, airdrop or promise of future rewards.

4. A public record is not a trustless answer

The chain makes the submitted record inspectable. It does not make an ambiguous question precise, prove a person is unique, or guarantee that a human resolver is correct.

The current resolver is the pilot contract owner. The contract enforces a closing time and one-time resolution, but does not automatically verify that the chosen outcome matches the external source. Resolution requires trust in the operator. There is no independent onchain dispute process in this release.

Each question fixes its source and rules before opening. The price questions specify a Coinbase Exchange daily candle, UTC observation window, strict comparison and a seven-day missing-data cancellation condition. The chain-activity question specifies a canonical block and timestamp condition, with cancellation for a reset or prolonged data outage. Read the complete rules on the individual question; a headline alone is not the settlement definition.

An ambiguous or unavailable source should lead to cancellation under the stated rules. Cancellation preserves the call's existence while keeping that question out of resolved/correct totals. Better evidence publication, independent review and a documented dispute path are prerequisites for a more mature product. They are roadmap work, not present guarantees.

The contract has not undergone an independent professional security audit. This is an experimental testnet service. Testnets can reset, data access can fail, and long-term availability is not guaranteed. “A proof of thought” refers to an inspectable record of the submitted view in this deployed testnet system. It is neither proof of correctness nor a guarantee that a test network exists forever.

5. Confidence is a view, not a price

Selecting YES with 70% confidence means you assign 70% probability to YES. Selecting NO with 70% confidence means you assign 30% probability to YES. Neither number is an executable price, investment recommendation or expected return.

The board's YES percentage, when live, is the share of recorded calls choosing YES. It is not confidence-weighted and is not a representative survey or market-implied probability. No-calls states and illustrative previews are labeled separately. A small sample should never be presented as collective certainty.

The current record counts outcomes. Richer calibration analysis is planned: comparing probability estimates with eventual results, showing sample sizes and question mix, and preserving the complete history. A winning streak is not proof of investment skill.

6. Why Robinhood Chain

Robinhood Chain offers an Ethereum-compatible environment, familiar wallet tools and a financial-application ecosystem. The pilot uses its testnet to make the record loop tangible before a production decision.

Convistelle is independent. It is not affiliated with, sponsored by, or endorsed by Robinhood. Building on the chain does not provide access to a Robinhood account, Stock Tokens, investment protections or a licensed trading service. No asset execution is part of this pilot.

The operational test has a forecast transaction and a resolution transaction. They demonstrate the pilot mechanism; they are not an audit or organic activity.

The current public brand is Convistelle. Existing onchain text and deployment records may retain the former name, Forevane. This rebrand changes the interface and launch materials; it preserves the deployed contract, transaction history and immutable question definitions.

7. Where we are headed

Stage Intended work Evidence required before expanding
Now: public testnet Clear questions, wallet records, owner-resolved outcomes, honest product feedback Reliable end-to-end use and understandable rules
Next: community pilots Recurring forecasting rounds, moderator playbooks, evidence-based recaps Communities return for a second round without financial incentives
Then: useful analysis Complete exports, calibration, community workspaces, opt-in chat integrations Retention and willingness to pay for the workflow
Later: portable records Partner embeds, stable schemas and contracted API access Data quality, privacy controls and customer demand

These are proposed stages, not announced delivery dates. Mainnet would require a separate production readiness decision, independent security review, stronger administration, resolution operations and legal review. Going mainnet would not automatically introduce monetary stakes.

The proposed business is software subscriptions for communities and people who want better analysis. Public records should remain inspectable. Payment must never buy a favorable outcome, hide a bad call or purchase a ranking. Financial execution is outside the base plan.

Read the full business plan (PDF) for customer hypotheses, unit economics, operating responsibilities, a 90-day execution schedule and explicit stop-or-narrow decision gates. All commercial figures there are assumptions, not existing revenue or traction.

8. A few principles we intend to keep

  • Show the original view. Timing, confidence and rules belong beside the result.
  • Keep the full history. Wrong calls and cancellations are part of an honest record.
  • Make room for disagreement. A shared question should not require a shared answer.
  • Explain the limits. A timestamp is evidence of a submission, not proof of truth.
  • Earn the next step. Build useful habits before adding incentives, complexity or financial exposure.

Make your view count: inspect the evidence, state your confidence, and return to what happened.
